status: DECISION RECORD (W2 AREA, D-AREA), MODEL ESTIMATE: every area number is a courtyard sum computed by pcb/partition_budget.py into pcb/partition-budget.json; no placement, no proof-fit; hardware gates stay OPEN

decision.summary: Four main boards: PWR-A (plate-bonded L, 7910 mm2), PWR-B (mezzanine on the PWR-A footprint, Samtec LSHM-150-02.5 pair J208/J209, 5.00 mm stack (W2 B2B; was QSH/QTH-060-01)), RF (unchanged) and a two-sided CTRL; harness headers consolidated per destination and exit zone. Working partition (a): the draft PWR-B list, with the LNB OVP comparator (U220 group) kept on PWR-A next to U212 so that E1_SW and the LNB LDO rail do not cross. Computed verdict (MODEL ESTIMATE): no evaluated partition fits at 1.8. Candidate (a) gives PWR-A 0.640 and PWR-B 0.427 (usable / demand), because every PWR-A part taller than hA and every PWR-A power header costs PWR-B a window or an edge strip (3.8k + 1.4k of the 7.6k outline). CTRL two-sided gives top 1.003 and bottom 0.979 by area, and five CTRL bottom headers have no height-valid variant under the depth cap (ctrl_headers_unresolved), so CTRL is NOT FIT as well.
decision.why_a: (a) and (b) leave almost the same total shortfall (about 7.3k mm2 at 1.8), but (a) needs 53 B2B contacts against 81, moves no fused high-current internal net (E2_J21_FUSED) across the boards, and keeps the J21/display/Lime/AUX12 eFuses with their fuse holders and bulk capacitors; moving more groups to PWR-B overfills PWR-B, whose usable area is set by the windows
decision.shortfall_note: demand at 1.8 minus usable area, candidate (a), pcb/partition-budget.json; the PWR harness headers alone are 2.7k mm2 raw (about 4.9k at 1.8), two thirds of the PWR shortfall
decision.ctrl_headers_unresolved_note: W2 GR-3 (graph refs, real KiCad 10.0.7 courtyards): J304 (S01 IDC box XDFH-0254-2*20P: drawing and mated height with the IDC socket not read, so header_families.IDC_top h is TBD and pcb/partition-budget.json rejects it as height not read; the 9.1 mm body of the reference Würth WR-BHD 61204021621 alone, mechanical/params/parts.json harness_headers IDC_top, already gives 9.1 + 1.0 - 3.9 = 6.2 > cap 6.0) and J313 (KK 22-27-2031, height not read) have no height-valid place over BMS/IP2368; they stay counted on the CTRL bottom and need a CTRL zone with free height >= h + 1.0 mm (MECH-3) or a lower part with a read drawing. The Micro-Fit LAB5 and blower headers are right-angle 43650-0400/-0200 (J305, J314; mated 6.98 mm, dz 4.08); the former X25P1-CTRL no longer exists (GR-1)
rejected: (b) switch groups on PWR-B: PWR-A 0.701, PWR-B 0.364, 81 contacts and E2_J21_FUSED (4 A) across the boards

(c) Pololu modules off PWR-A on plate standoffs: PWR-A 0.721, PWR-B 0.701, still short, and no plate location exists (front face full, build/15 'Розмір'; behind the left leg sit the HF+ can and the RF bay, mechanical/generated/fit-report.md layout); a cut-out in the L for them saves nothing
bigger single PWR board or larger face: the face is fixed by the plan (D-ENV width unchanged, STACK.md:109 HMI layouts); depth growth adds no area
radials or headers on the RF board: RF max height 5.5 (mechanical/params/boards.json:91) and constraints DC-02/RF-01 (pcb/generated/constraints.json:52-92)
(h8) hB 8.0 instead of 5.5: PWR-A 0.650, PWR-B 0.491 for 2.5 mm more depth (dz_mezz 4.6); still short, and the radials (11.0-11.5 mm) stay above it

(s8) the 8.00 mm stack (W2 B2B: two LSHM-150-04.0 halves; AREA: QTH-060-02 with QSH-060-01; hA 7.5, window ceiling 15.1 mm): PWR-B 0.427 -> 0.560 (windows 3.8k -> 3.1k mm2: the polymer capacitors, XAL6060, SRR1260 and C506 no longer need one; the Keystone 3568 holders keep theirs, their height being a lower bound), PWR-A unchanged 0.640, dz_mezz 5.1 <= cap 6.0. It is the strongest PWR-B lever but is not adopted alone: PWR-B stays short, it costs 3 mm more depth, and the 8.00 mm part is thin in stock (W2 B2B: LSHM-150-04.0-L-DV-A-N-K-TR C5753117 14 on 2026-11-07; AREA: QTH-060-02-L-D-A 0, -K 33, -TR 5); it goes into next_decision together with a PWR-A lever (s8c)

(a80) the 80-contact LSHM-140 pair (W2 B2B; it replaces (a60), the 60-contact QSH-030/QTH-030 pair of AREA): PWR-A 0.664, PWR-B 0.503 against 0.661 / 0.497 of the LSHM-150 (56 mm2 less demand at 1.8 on each board); it takes the 69 contacts of (a) but misses the spare rule (83 > 80 under b2b.guard_rule, W2 B2B review R2), and neither size covers (b) (119)

(am) the five unresolved CTRL bottom headers moved to PWR-A (rule_gr3: the function moves to PWR): PWR-A 0.566, PWR-B 0.245 (their edge strips), CTRL top 1.218, bottom 1.460; S01 (IDC to the Q6A) and the LAB5 input of CTRL cannot move by function, so their area stays on CTRL
decision.next_decision: OPEN for INT/owner (integration_plan step 8, F2): the PWR function needs about 7.3k mm2 more board area at 1.8 than PWR-A + PWR-B give in the plan's face, or a smaller PWR connector/circuit set. Best combinations evaluated (MODEL ESTIMATE): s8c (8.00 mm stack + Pololu modules off PWR-A + PCB-REAR) PWR-A 0.755, PWR-B 1.012; w2 (hypothetical radials <= hB + (b) + Pololu off) PWR-A 0.874. PWR-A stays short in every one (about 2.5k mm2 at best, s8c), so the owner lever is PWR-A area (a larger or second rear board, or face growth) or fewer PWR-A parts and headers; the 8.00 mm stack (s8, dz_mezz 5.1) is the PWR-B lever to take with it. GR-3, MECH-3 and the board packages implement (a) as the working partition; the real placement fill of PCB-PWRA-1/2 and PCB-PWRB is the trigger record.

mpn.why: W2 B2B (orchestrator decision, 07.11.2026): one hermaphroditic part on both boards instead of the QSH/QTH pair of W2 AREA (b2b.superseded). For QSH/QTH the land patterns are readable (Samtec Rev M drawings, b2b.superseded.src), but no first-party document states the QTH-over-QSH mating pin map, so the pin map would stay an owner action. The LSHM has an official KiCad 10.0.7 footprint that matches the Samtec Rev G drawing, a documented mating map (print Rev Z note 4, b2b.mating_map), a smaller courtyard (30.70 x 6.20 against 41.77 x 7.99 and 40.50 x 7.61) and one MPN for both halves. Cost: no ground plane, so every rail contact has its GND return beside it and the rail block is guarded by GND (guard_rule, W2 B2B review R2). 100 contacts (-150) against the 80 of LSHM-140 (candidate a80): (a) needs 69, 83 with the spare; the -150 keeps 17 contacts beyond the spare rule for nets that placement may add, the -140 takes the 69 but misses the spare rule (83 > 80); the -150 costs 0.003 of the PWR-A and 0.006 of the PWR-B ratio at 1.8 (MODEL ESTIMATE). Neither covers (b), which needs 119 contacts (143 with the spare): if the owner moves the switch groups to PWR-B, the B2B choice reopens. Two -02.5 halves give the 5.00 mm stack, so hA, the windows and the F45 standoffs stay. Stock is evidence only

b2b.rule: contacts per crossing power net = ceil(I_protection / b2b_i_pin_A), I_protection from tools/assembly_data.py NET_CURRENT or net_current_extra; every other crossing net 1 contact; plus the GND contacts of guard_rule (W2 B2B: the LSHM has no ground plane; review R2): gnd_pins_per_power_contact (1) beside every rail contact (power contacts, sense/supply taps and rail nodes) and the guard contacts; Kelvin and precision nets (shunt nets, INA inputs, precision divider mid-points) never cross except declared_sense_pairs and sense_taps; pcb/prepare.py writes pcb/generated/b2b-nets.json by the same rule, with the contact map
b2b.i_pin_note: b2b_i_pin_A 1.0 A per contact is a design derating: half the Samtec LSHM rating of 2 A per pin, which spec Rev H states for one pin powered per row only; in the power block every column carries a power contact and its GND return, and neighbouring columns carry current at the same time. Samtec gives no rating for many powered pins, so 1.0 A is not a rating; the B2B temperature rise is a bench gate (OPEN)

mating_map.formula: pin n of J208 (PWR-A) meets pin n+1 of J209 (PWR-B) for n odd and pin n-1 for n even; the map is its own inverse
mating_map.source: Samtec print Rev Z note 4 (https://suddendocs.samtec.com/prints/lshm-1xx-xx.x-xxx-dv-a-x-x-tr-mkt.pdf, read 2026-11-07): pin 01 mates contact 02 of the other LSHM-DV
mating_map.derivation: both halves are the same footprint (odd pads in one row, even pads in the other, pads 2k-1 and 2k at the same x); pin 01 meeting contact 02 means the upper half is turned over about the strip axis, so every column k pairs 2k-1 with 2k; pcb/tests/test_b2b_map.py checks it on the vendored footprint
mating_map.placement: J209 on the PWR-B bottom over J208 (same centre in the shared PWR-A/PWR-B frame), so that its pad m lies over J208 pad b2b_mate(m): seen from the PWR-A top, J209 is J208 mirrored about the strip axis (y -> -y in the J208 frame); its pin-1 row lies over the even row of J208 and its alignment holes at (+/-13.5, +0.85) against (+/-13.5, -0.85) of J208. A bottom-side footprint flipped top/bottom, or flipped left/right and turned 180 degrees, is that mirror; pcb/check_boards.py b2b with pin_map from b2b-nets.json contacts checks it

b2b.pin_map_rule: pcb/prepare.py b2b_contacts (W2 B2B, review R2; sense pairs at the end since 11.11.2026): J208 column c = contacts 2c-1 (odd row) and 2c (even row). Each declared sense pair takes one column at the end of the strip (the last column, a further pair two columns before it), with a GND guard column before it. From contact 1: the rail block of guard_rule, one column per rail contact in the order rail_order, which lists the rail contacts column by column (a net listed once keeps its contacts side by side; unlisted rails after it, by name), the rail contact on the odd row in odd columns and on the even row in even columns, its GND return in the other row of the column; one GND guard after the last rail contact, in its row; the other crossing nets in name order, one per column on the free even contacts in contact order (the even row of J208 = the odd row of J209), one contact each; the rest spare (nc in the graph). For (a): 1-42 the rail block (21 columns), 43 guard, 44-86 even the 22 signal nets (columns 22-43, their odd contacts spare), 87-96 spare, 97-98 guard, 99-100 the LNA4 sense pair. J209 contact m carries the net of J208 contact b2b_mate(m). python -I pcb/write_b2b_graph.py writes the map into the graph refs (--check compares). Design value. Why the sense pair sits at the end: on the PWR-B board of record (build/kicad/boards/PWR_B/make_spec.py) J209 lies on the bottom side turned so that column 50 is under the ch4 shunt R246 and column 1 next to the end of the LAB5 trunk; the Kelvin pair then reaches its shunt, the rail block the LAB5 switches and the left LNA channels, and the signal block, all in the J209 row that faces them, the harness headers J202/J203 below it, without crossing the strip (route run 43103920112 with signals in both rows left two signals to J202 open). PWR-A places J208 under J209 (b2b.mating_map)

b2b.guard_rule: W2 B2B review R2 (07.11.2026): the pads are 0.30 mm wide at 0.50 mm pitch, so neighbouring pads of a row are 0.20 mm apart (b2b.footprint, Samtec Rev G), and a solder bridge between them is the likely defect at this pitch. So no contact at a supply-rail potential has a neighbour in its row other than GND. (1) Rail contacts are the power contacts, the sense/supply taps and the rail nodes: crossing nets that a resistor below rail_node_max_ohm joins to a net other than GND, such as the 0.22 ohm damper nodes (BIAS_CH1_DAMP: R232 from BIAS_CH1, C235 47 uF to GND; pcb/prepare.py low_ohm_links). Each takes one column: the rail contact on the odd row in odd columns and on the even row in even columns, its GND return in the other row (a checkerboard), in the order rail_order. (2) One GND guard contact follows the last rail contact in its row. (3) Each declared sense pair (at the potential of its rail) takes one column at the end of the strip, with a GND guard column before it. A bridge from a rail contact can then only short that rail to GND, where its protection (tools/assembly_data.py NET_CURRENT) acts; it cannot join two rails, a rail and a sense line, or a rail and a signal line. rail_order puts 3V3_Q6A first and the 12-13.8 V rails of the net names (AUX12, LNB13V2, the BONI13V8 tap and BONI13V8_PORT) last. Between them (since 11.11.2026, for the PWR-B board of record, where J209 is turned so that the even columns form the contact row facing the LAB5 trunk and the harness headers below the strip and the odd columns the row facing the top-edge headers): the even columns carry the four LAB5 contacts next to the trunk and the rails that leave towards the west and the bottom (BIAS_CH2_DAMP, one LNA4V5, BIAS_CH3_DAMP, VBUS_LABPORT), the odd columns the rails that leave upwards (the other LNA4V5, BIAS_CH1_DAMP, E2_SB_DAMP, VBUS_RTLB_DAMP, VBUS_HFP, BIAS_CH4_DAMP, both LAB5_RLY). The damper nodes also get their AC return beside them: the 47 uF capacitor sits on PWR-A and the 0.22 ohm resistor on PWR-B. Cost for (a): 10 GND contacts more than one per power contact (6 rail nodes, 1 tap, 3 guards). Design value; signal nets still neighbour signal nets
